subject: devon
title: Revert restores git commit, event log, and agent chat history as one tri-consistent unit, with on-resume drift reconciliation
evidence: devon_agent/session.py:229-252 (revert), devon_agent/config.py:16-25 (Checkpoint holds commit_hash+event_id+agent_history+state), devon_agent/session.py:267-660 (git_setup load: detects user commits/unstaged changes made while agent was away and injects them into chat history), session.py:1199-1298 (merge = patch of agent-branch diff onto user branch)
one_why: Nuance vs existing checkpoint-revert entries: devon never lets code and narrative state diverge across revert/resume - the 400-LOC reconcile pass means a user commit made mid-session is surfaced to the agent instead of silently conflicting; the git-branch-isolation-plus-patch-merge shape is the 2024 ancestor of aider-lineage checkpointing, but the tri-consistency discipline is worth naming.

subject: devon
title: Loop consumes an append-only producer/consumer event list persisted to sqlite every model step
evidence: devon_agent/session.py:788-843 (run_event_loop walks indexed event list), session.py:845-1101 (step_event match on event type), session.py:1191-1197 (persist after every predict)
one_why: Early (2024) crude instance of the kimi-code/nausicaa concept: no replay validation, no idempotency keys, mutable python list + sleep-polling - included to date the concept family, not to port; the durability machinery that makes the later entries valuable is absent.

subject: devon
title: No approval gate of any kind: model-parsed commands dispatch straight into a persistent interactive bash
evidence: devon_agent/session.py:913-963 (ToolRequest case calls env.tools[tool_name] directly), devon_agent/tools/shelltool.py:30-35 (writes fn_name+args into env.execute), devon_agent/environments/shell_environment.py:94-100 (persistent /bin/bash -l stdin), session.py:967-998 (unknown tool names fall through to the same shell)
one_why: grep for approve/confirm/permission across devon_agent finds only git-branch bookkeeping and prompt text - nothing binds anything; the devon_agent branch confines file edits for recovery but shell commands can escape it freely, so even the branch affordance is not a security boundary.

subject: devon
title: FastAPI control plane binds 0.0.0.0 with zero auth, exposing session-start and event-injection endpoints that drive arbitrary local bash
evidence: devon_agent/__main__.py:41 (uvicorn host="0.0.0.0"), devon_agent/server.py:238 (POST /sessions), :331 (PATCH start), :496 (POST event), :471 (POST response)
one_why: Combined with devon-3 this is LAN-RCE by design: no token, no origin check beyond a CORS list for localhost UIs, and the events API accepts raw task/tool text that the loop executes; least-privilege would be 127.0.0.1 plus a session token, both trivial fixes the dead repo never got.

subject: devon
title: Zero context management: full chat history resent every turn (openai path) or flattened into a per-request transcript rebuild (anthropic path), no compaction, counting, or overflow handling anywhere
evidence: devon_agent/agents/conversational_agent.py:151,169 (messages = history + last prompt), :119 (anthropic_history_to_bash_history rebuild), grep -iE 'compact|context.?window|trim|tiktoken' devon_agent => no product hits; only editor-view pagination conversational_agent.py:81-101
one_why: Baseline below codel's 1-rung (which at least caps prompt length and asks the human): sessions fail only when the provider hard-errors, and the anthropic flat-rebuild makes every request a full-price prompt-cache miss, so cost is quadratic in both turns and dollars.

subject: devon
title: ~600 LOC of pytest with no CI runner at all; one suite is 163 lines of commented-out code
evidence: devon_agent/test/ (8 files, 597 LOC total), devon_agent/test/test_event_system.py:1-163 (entirely commented), .github/ contains only autopr.yaml (no workflows dir)
one_why: The tests that exist are honest behavior tests (test_edit_tool.py applies edit blocks against a temp-dir shell env), which makes their never-running status the whole story: no green/red signal has ever gated a commit.

subject: devon
title: PostHog telemetry on by default with hardcoded project key; opt-out only on exact env string "true"
evidence: devon_agent/utils/telemetry.py:106-113 (DEVON_TELEMETRY_DISABLED compared == "true"; posthog.project_api_key hardcoded), utils/telemetry.py:65 (persistent user id in ~/.cache/devon)
one_why: Nuance vs other default-on entries: the opt-out itself is fail-open - DEVON_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1/TRUE/on all leave telemetry enabled because only lowercase "true" disables it.

subject: devon
title: Session class fuses loop, ~400-line git state machine, and merge logic; git_setup repeats one error-handling block ~15 times
evidence: devon_agent/session.py:1299 LOC total, git_setup session.py:267-660 with the identical nogit/resolvedError retry ladder at :292,308,319,333,348,363,396,412,429,459...
one_why: Same shape as other god-file-loop entries but with a distinct cost: the duplicated git error ladder means any new git operation must hand-copy four branches of control flow, which is why reconcile bugs hide in the load path untested.

subject: devon
title: README license badge advertises Apache-2.0 while LICENSE is AGPL-3.0
evidence: README.md:12 (alt="Apache 2.0 License" badge), LICENSE:1-2 (GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3)
one_why: Nuance vs capability drift: this is license drift - downstream users citing the README could adopt AGPL code believing it permissive; for our study it also means any concept porting must stay clean-room regardless of what the badge claims.
